title: Test small object visibility in complex scenes
description: The jade figurine was missing/hard to see in the Hades scene. Test various approaches: stronger emphasis in prompt, foreground placement language, larger relative size descriptions. Determine if small important objects can be reliably rendered.
notes:
## Small Object Visibility Test Results

All three approaches successfully render small objects prominently:

### Test Results
1. **Strong emphasis** (IMPORTANT, focal point, glows): Object becomes large, glowing, centered
2. **Foreground placement** (bottom third, close to camera): Good size, proper depth composition  
3. **Size + shape description** (palm-sized, 6 inches, seated Buddha): **BEST** - produces detailed, recognizable object

### Recommendations for FrotzLM prompts:
- Use specific size descriptions ("palm-sized", "6 inches tall")
- Describe the object's shape/form ("seated Buddha", "carved jade")
- Add lighting interaction ("catches torchlight", "stands out against")
- Avoid vague "small" - use relative or absolute sizes instead

### Original Issue
The hades scene prompt said "small exquisite jade figurine" which was too vague. Better: "A palm-sized jade figurine carved as a seated figure, its green surface catching the dim light"

### Conclusion
Small objects CAN be reliably rendered when prompts include specific size, shape, and visual contrast descriptions.

title: Test cross-scene consistency without references
description: Generate the same object/character in multiple different scenes using only text prompts (no reference images). Measure visual drift. This establishes the baseline for how much reference images help.
close_reason: Cross-scene consistency test complete. Generated brass lantern in 3 different scenes (dungeon, forest, tavern) using text-only prompts. Results: Text-only achieves reasonable internal consistency (all produced hurricane-style lanterns), but shows significant drift from any specific design intent. Compared to reference-based generation (frotzlm-lp1.4), text-only prompts cannot maintain a specific object design across scenes. Conclusion: Reference images are essential for Zork illustration consistency. Test images saved to test_consistency/.

title: Evaluate if additional tools needed (GLIGEN, ControlNet, etc.)
description: Based on composition and consistency test results, determine if OmniGen2 alone is sufficient or if we need to add: GLIGEN for bounding box layout control, ControlNet for structural guidance, IP-Adapter for stronger reference adherence, StoryDiffusion for cross-scene consistency.
close_reason: Evaluation complete. OmniGen2 is SUFFICIENT for FrotzLM without additional tools. Spatial composition, reference adherence, and multi-reference generation all work well. Only limitation is object counting above 5 (use spatial positioning instead). Reference images are essential for cross-scene consistency - text-only prompts drift. No need for GLIGEN, ControlNet, IP-Adapter, or StoryDiffusion.
